blocks.text: "[12/01, 08:27, Tzlil]: Beautiful work, well done, both of you! The only thing is that Tilly's footsteps don't sound like the footsteps of a young girl in the 1930s. More generally, I think she should be wearing small heels — they clearly signal gender. More specifically, this is a place that's meant to train young girls to become proper ladies, so it feels strange to hear relatively soft footsteps with a sole that sounds modern. It should be wood on a wooden floor." — Tzlil

"In some cases, the choice of sounds required historical details we did not know with certainty but about which we could make an educated guess. For example, we did not know what kind of shoes the girls wore, an issue that might sound insignificant, but is central in the context of the podcast where footsteps carry so much of the narrative. We did know, however, that the agenda of Huize Dina was to turn girls from difficult backgrounds into well behaved young ladies and we also found a photograph of girls from Huize Dina wearing wooden-soled, high-heeled shoes. This photograph gave us a good clue as to what their footsteps might have sounded like." — Amit

"Other decisions concerned the girls' behavior — the way each character speaks or reacts to what is being said to her or in her presence. The decisions we made, though necessarily fictional, were nevertheless grounded in thorough research of the girls' lives as reflected in the archive, as well as on the detailed psychological reports about their personalities that formed part of the archive." — Amit
